Hi Aditya,

Quick context: we are coming up on our Nov renewal but we have an expected 30% increase in inference consumption starting July due to a new feature launch. Procurement asked whether we can expand capacity mid-term and either co-term to Nov or have a temporary top-up until renewal.

Two asks: 1) a simple proposal for a mid-term uplift (cost delta, impact to unit pricing), and 2) whether Redwood will allow co-terming the uplift to our Nov renewal so invoicing is consolidated. We also have a tight procurement window — legal wants any amendment queued by the end of May.

Can you share options? We prefer a path that minimizes short-term cash impact but keeps unit economics favorable.

Thanks,
Priyanka

OpenWell Health

Priyanka — thank you for the context and timeline. Quick reply with three pragmatic options (details attached in the spreadsheet):

1) Staged top-up (preferred for cash-sensitive customers)
   - Immediate add-on for July–Nov at a slightly higher unit price (+7% to current effective rate)
   - Add-on billed monthly; credit applied at renewal to proportionally reduce next-year committed units if you annualize

2) Co-termed amendment (preferred for simplicity)
   - Add the uplift now, co-term everything to Nov with an amended annual commitment
   - We can offer a 10% blended discount on the incremental uplift if you commit to annualize at renewal

3) Voucher/bridge credit (for short-run spikes)
   - Pre-purchase voucher credits at a 5% discount to cover the uplift months, converted to committed units if you choose to annualize

I've attached OpenWell_Uplift_Options_Q2.xlsx with exact numbers for a 30% uplift and three scenarios (monthly billing, co-term annualize, voucher).

Next steps I propose: 1) procurement/legal reviews the spreadsheet; 2) we loop in Monica (finance) and Grace (CS onboarding) for billing and implementation timelines; 3) sign a short amendment or DocuSign voucher by May 28.

If you want, I can do a 30-minute walk-through tomorrow to walk through the numbers and preferred path.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Renewals & Expansion
Redwood Inference

Looping in finance notes and a counter-proposal for negotiation:

- We can move from 10% -> 12% blended discount on the incremental uplift if OpenWell commits to annualize at renewal AND agrees to a 12-month notice for any destructive decommit (standard). The 12% requires a minimum 9-month annualization window (effectively Nov renewal).
- For staged top-up (option 1), we will provide a usage reconciliation report (token-level ingest/consumption summary) monthly. Any unused add-on units can be credited, but credits expire at renewal unless annualized.
- Voucher option: we can increase voucher discount to 7% for a pre-pay covering at least 3 months of uplift.

Operational notes for Grace: if they pick staged top-up, we need a 2-week runbook: model pinning for the uplift pool, capacity notes, and KV cache warm-up windows.

If Aditya gets procurement to signal which path they prefer in the walkthrough, Monica and I can prep the amendment and payment terms.

- Monica
